spans.text: The Medicare Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) is a critical time for beneficiaries to review and make changes to their healthcare coverage. Understanding the benefits of this period can help you make the best decisions for your healthcare needs. AEP runs from October 15 to December 7 each year.

During AEP, you can switch from Original Medicare to Medicare Advantage or vice versa. You can also switch between Medicare Advantage plans, join a Medicare Part D prescription drug plan, or switch between Part D plans. This flexibility allows you to adjust your coverage based on changes in your health or financial situation.

One of the main benefits of AEP is the ability to review and compare different plans. Each year, insurance companies may change the benefits, costs, and networks of their plans. Reviewing these changes can help you find a plan that offers the best coverage and value for your needs.

Cost is a significant factor to consider during AEP. Medicare Advantage and Part D plans can vary widely in premiums, deductibles, and copayments. By comparing different plans, you can find one that fits your budget and provides the coverage you need.

Network flexibility is another important consideration. Medicare Advantage plans often have networks of preferred providers, which can change each year. During AEP, you can review the networks of different plans to ensure your preferred doctors and hospitals are included.

Prescription drug coverage is also a key factor. Each Part D plan has a formulary, or list of covered drugs, which can change annually. Reviewing the formularies of different plans during AEP can help you ensure your medications are covered and find a plan that offers the best value.
